title: Enforcement Powers for Fair Employment Breaches
what_it_is: Enforcement Powers for Fair Employment Breaches

sections.label: Age and pregnancy dismissal protection
sections.summary: The RRA bars age-based dismissal, while the EA and CDCA protect pregnant female employees from dismissal without sufficient cause.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Under the Retirement and Re-employment Act (RRA), an employer cannot dismiss an employee on the grounds of age.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The Employment Act (EA) and Child Development Co-Savings Act (CDCA) also protect female employees from being dismissed without sufficient cause during any stage of their pregnancy.

sections.label: MOM enforcement against employment discrimination
sections.summary: MOM will take enforcement actions under the RRA, EA or CDCA and can suspend work pass privileges for unfair employment practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: MOM takes a serious view of all forms of employment discrimination and, if employers are found to have engaged in such unfair employment practices, MOM will take appropriate enforcement actions under the RRA, EA or CDCA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: MOM can also suspend their work pass privileges under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act.

sections.label: Age and gender complaint numbers
sections.summary: Complaints on attributes besides nationality, such as age and gender, remained stable, accounting for about 20% of total complaints in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: For complaints related to attributes besides nationality, for example, age and gender, the number has remained stable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Age- and gender-related complaints accounted for about 20% of total complaints in 2015.

sections.label: Anti-discrimination laws as final option
sections.summary: The Member asked whether MOM would consider workplace anti-discrimination laws as a final option if discrimination cases increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I wanted to ask the Minister of State, bearing in mind that we have the RRA, the EA, as well as the CDCA, would MOM look at implementing specific workplace-related anti-discrimination laws as a final option, if and when cases of discrimination do increase in the coming years?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: So far, the number of complaints has remained stable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: TAFEP, as an advocate for fair employment practices, is enhancing and strengthening its educational efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: We believe that this approach has worked so far as most employers engaged by TAFEP did rectify their employment practices.
